source.title: TIDE : Temporal-Aware Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Diffusion Transformers in Image Generation
source.authors: Victor Shea-Jay Huang; Le Zhuo; Yi Xin; Zhaokai Wang; Fu-Yun Wang; Yuchi Wang; Ren-Rui Zhang; Peng Gao; Hongsheng Li

record.file_problem: The paper text is present; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses sparse autoencoders, motivated in part by superposition, to interpret and edit diffusion-transformer activations. It does not test the claimed superposition geometry or capacity account.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE/TIDE reconstruction metrics and downstream image-generation results, but these evaluate its proposed method rather than whether features overlap as superposition predicts. Its qualitative feature examples are recorded under fits_no_version because they concern sparse features in diffusion transformers, not the LLM claim versions. Cited claims about superposition are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The paper applies top-k SAEs (motivated by superposition) to diffusion-transformer activations and reports its method's reconstruction, diffusion-loss, FID/AlignScore and safety results plus qualitative feature examples. It never measures feature overlap, capacity competition, polysemanticity origins, SAE feature completeness/stability, or feature dimensionality. V4 names LLMs; DiT sparse-feature recovery is a different kind of system and is evaluated only as method performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: TIDE extracts interpretable multi-level features from DiTs, supports editing and safe editing with small quality cost, generalizes across backbones, and complex editing remains limited by sparsity constraints.
record.recipe_differences: TIDE is a top-k sparse autoencoder with timestep-dependent modulation, trained on diffusion-transformer activations; it does not reproduce the original toy-model method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that outcomes vary with sparsity, latent dimension, token sampling, DiT layer, and diffusion backbone; these are TIDE and image-generation evaluations, not tests of the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: TIDE (timestep-modulated top-k SAE) on PixArt-alpha activations yields qualitatively interpretable 3D-, class- and semantic-level features; reconstruction cosine ~0.97 at 16d latents with 5% sparsity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse autoencoders recover interpretable, hierarchical sparse features from diffusion-transformer activations with high reconstruction fidelity.

record.problems: The paper does not directly measure feature overlap, orthogonality, capacity competition, completeness, stability, or canonicality. Its feature examples are qualitative, and the reported reconstruction and generation metrics evaluate TIDE rather than the superposition claim.
record.rows_left_out: Reconstruction, diffusion-loss, image-quality, editing, and safety results were left out because they evaluate TIDE's method or applications rather than the claim's feature geometry or capacity account (Tables 1 and 2; Fig. 4).

untested.parts: Toy networks, near-orthogonal overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transition, geometry.
Capacity competition as cause of polysemanticity.
Feature spreading across neurons or SAE recovery of sparse features in LLMs (study is on image DiTs only, and reports SAE performance metrics rather than evidence about superposition).
Completeness, stability, canonicality of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: Superposition is cited only as motivation in related work (Elhage et al. 2022). Feature-identification procedure in the 'Diffusion Really Learned Features' section is vaguely described (pooled activations and token similarity) with no quantitative interpretability evaluation. Reconstruction/FID/safety results are method evaluations, correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature overlap and near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemantic neurons result from competition for capacity or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure.
LLM feature distribution across neurons and SAE recovery of sparse features in LLMs.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: PixArt-XL-2-1024-MS
rows.operation_detail: TIDE feature extraction and similarity-based identification of 3D-level concepts
rows.measure: Qualitative feature examples and associated image characteristics
rows.value: The paper reports features such as “far,” “near,” and “shadow,” associated with foreground-background relationships.
rows.note: This describes sparse features extracted from a diffusion transformer; it does not measure the overlap geometry in the claim.
rows.check: Qualitative feature examples in a diffusion transformer; no measure of superposition or SAE canonicality. Also the method described is pooled-activation similarity, not clearly an SAE-latent analysis.

rows.subject: PixArt-XL-2-1024-MS
rows.operation_detail: TIDE feature extraction and similarity-based identification of class-level concepts
rows.measure: Qualitative feature examples and reported hierarchical associations
rows.value: The paper reports class-related feature examples including “Rococo” with house, window, and door, and “eagle” with bird, fly, and beak.
rows.note: These examples do not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
rows.check: Qualitative class-level examples; no baseline, no measure bearing on any version.

rows.subject: PixArt-XL-2-1024-MS
rows.operation_detail: TIDE feature extraction and similarity-based identification of semantic concepts and locations
rows.measure: Qualitative feature examples and spatial localization
rows.value: The paper reports identifying a localized semantic feature such as an eagle's beak.
rows.note: This is qualitative evidence about features in a diffusion transformer, not evidence about superposition geometry or canonicality.
rows.check: Qualitative localization example; no measure bearing on any version.
